rationale_highlights: the systemic factors that have played a part in the over-representation of aboriginal people in the prison system have played some part in bringing him before the Court
these factors do serve to moderate his moral culpability somewhat
even after an appropriate allowance for them his level of culpability for this very serious act of violence remains high
even after attributing some moderating effect to the contributing factors arising from his aboriginal background, his level of moral blameworthiness for this offence is still high

Mr. Rommann was injured. He suffered a number of knife wounds

rationale_highlights: Factors which mitigate are (1) the offender's youth, (2) the offender's lack of a prior criminal record, (3) the offender's aboriginal ancestry
Recent decisions in the Supreme Court of Canada make it clear that the Gladue factors apply regardless of the seriousness of an offence

I am bound to apply section 718.2(e), recognizing that while systemic and background factors of aboriginal person do not operate as an excuse or justification for criminal conduct, they do provide necessary context to enable the court to determine an appropriate sentence
note: Ancestry listed as mitigating; effect on sentence not detailed.
